title: When must a company in Japan appoint a safe driving manager and run alcohol checks?
seoTitle: Japan safe driving manager and alcohol
description: Japan's Road Traffic Act safe driving manager rule: the five vehicle threshold, alcohol detector checks since December 1, 2023, records and annual training.
shortAnswer: Under Article 74-3 of Japan's Road Traffic Act, a company that uses five or more vehicles, or one vehicle seating 11 or more, at a site must appoint a safe driving manager there. Since December 1, 2023, the manager must check every driver for alcohol before and after driving, visually and with an alcohol detector, keep records for one year, and attend the course the Prefectural Public Safety Commission notifies.
keyTakeaways: The appointment threshold in Article 9-8 of the Enforcement Ordinance is one vehicle with a capacity of 11 or more, or five other vehicles, per site; motorcycles count as half a vehicle.
A vice safe driving manager is required from 20 vehicles, and one more for each additional 20 vehicles from 40.
Visual alcohol checks and records have been required since April 1, 2022; checks with an alcohol detector since December 1, 2023. Records are kept for one year.
Failing to appoint a manager is punishable by a fine of up to 500,000 yen, raised from 50,000 yen on October 1, 2022.
Managers must attend the statutory course when notified: 6 to 10 hours for a manager and 4 to 8 hours for a vice manager. The Tokyo Metropolitan Police Department runs it annually.
jurisdiction: Japan (national, administered by each Prefectural Public Safety Commission and prefectural police)
regulator: National Police Agency (NPA), Prefectural Public Safety Commissions and prefectural police
appliesTo: Any business or organization using company vehicles (white plate vehicles) above the threshold at a site, in any industry
Safe driving managers (anzen unten kanrisha) and vice safe driving managers
Employees who drive company vehicles for work
Staff designated to assist with alcohol checks when the manager is absent
Not licensed motor carriers with operation managers, which follow separate transport rules

sections.heading: Which law requires a safe driving manager in Japan?

blocks.text: The duty is in **Article 74-3** of the Road Traffic Act (Dōro Kōtsū Hō, Act No. 105 of 1960). It requires a vehicle user above a threshold to appoint a safe driving manager (anzen unten kanrisha) for each base of vehicle use, typically a site or office. The thresholds, qualifications and duties are set in Articles 9-8 to 9-11 of the [Road Traffic Act Enforcement Ordinance](https://laws.e-gov.go.jp/law/335M50000002060) (Prime Minister's Office Ordinance No. 60 of 1960).

The system applies to private vehicle users across all industries. As the [NPA system overview](https://www.npa.go.jp/bureau/traffic/anzenuntenkanrisya/pdf/seido.pdf) notes, sites of motor carriers that already appoint operation managers, second class freight forwarders and registered paid passenger transport operators are excluded. As at November 2026 the provisions cited here are the current text on e-Gov.

sections.heading: How many vehicles trigger the appointment duty?

blocks.text: A safe driving manager is required at a site that uses one vehicle with a passenger capacity of 11 or more, or five or more other vehicles. Article 9-8 also requires vice safe driving managers once a site reaches 20 vehicles, and counts each large or ordinary motorcycle as 0.5 vehicles.

Safe driving manager
Vice safe driving managers
rows: 1 vehicle seating 11 or more, or 5 to 19 other vehicles
blocks.caption: Appointment thresholds from Articles 9-8 and 9-11 of the Enforcement Ordinance

blocks.text: Article 74-3(5) requires the company to notify the Public Safety Commission with jurisdiction over the site within 15 days of appointing or dismissing a manager or vice manager.

A safe driving manager must be at least 20, or at least 30 where a vice manager is also appointed, and must have at least two years of practical experience in managing vehicle operation. Article 9-9 reduces the experience to one year for someone who has completed a course run by the Public Safety Commission, and allows the Commission to recognize equivalent ability.

A vice manager must be at least 20 and have one year of driving management experience or three years of driving experience. Both roles are barred for two years after a dismissal order and for two years after certain offenses, which the NPA overview lists as including drunk or drink driving, unlicensed driving, hit and run, and providing a vehicle or alcohol to a drunk driver, as well as ordering or tolerating offenses such as overloading or fatigued driving.

sections.heading: What must a safe driving manager do?

blocks.text: Article 9-10 lists nine duties. They cover driver fitness, operating plans, relief drivers, weather, roll calls, alcohol checks, alcohol check records, a driving log, and guidance to drivers. Article 74-3(2) adds traffic safety education for drivers, which Article 74-3(3) says must follow the national Traffic Safety Education Guidelines.

items: Understand each driver's aptitude, skills, knowledge and compliance with traffic law.
Draw up operating plans that prevent speeding, overloading, fatigued driving and other unsafe practices.
Arrange relief drivers for long distance or night driving where fatigue could make driving unsafe.
Give instructions and take safety measures in abnormal weather or disasters.
Hold a roll call or equivalent before driving to confirm vehicle inspections and check for fatigue, illness or other impairment.
Check drivers before and after driving for alcohol, visually and with an alcohol detector.
Record the alcohol check, keep the record for one year, and keep the detector in working order at all times.
Keep a driving log recording the driver, start and end times and distance.
Give drivers guidance on the skills and knowledge needed for safe driving.

blocks.text: Article 74-3(7) obliges the company to give the manager the authority and equipment needed for these duties. If it does not, the Public Safety Commission can order corrective measures under Article 74-3(8).

sections.heading: How do the alcohol check rules work?

blocks.text: Two dates matter. A 2021 amendment to the Enforcement Ordinance required visual alcohol checks and one year record keeping from April 1, 2022, and required checks with an alcohol detector, with records and detector maintenance. A 2023 amendment set December 1, 2023 as the start date for the detector requirement, as the NPA explains on its [page on the expanded duties](https://www.npa.go.jp/bureau/traffic/insyu/index-2.html).
The [NPA Q&A on alcohol checks](https://www.npa.go.jp/bureau/traffic/insyu/ankanQA.pdf) clarifies how the checks can be run:

items: Checks need not be repeated before and after every single trip. Checking at the start and end of a working day that includes driving is sufficient.

Face to face checks are the rule. For drivers who go directly to and from a site, a portable detector plus a camera, video call or phone call that lets the manager confirm the reading and the driver's condition is acceptable.

Any device that detects breath alcohol and shows the result by sound, light or number meets the requirement, but it must be used and maintained according to the manufacturer's instructions and checked regularly for faults.
Where the manager is absent, a vice manager, a contractor or another assistant may carry out the check, provided the manager has designated and instructed them and receives their reports.
Records must show the checker, driver, vehicle, date and time, method, result, instructions given and any other necessary matters.

blocks.text: An NPA circular of December 27, 2024 ([Circular Tei Kōki Hatsu No. 352](https://www.npa.go.jp/bureau/traffic/anzenuntenkanrisya/pdf/20241227ankankatyoutuutatu.pdf)) applied similar flexibility to roll calls, allowing remote methods by camera or phone where face to face checks are difficult. It also tells prefectural police to use the safe driving manager courses to make sure managers' duties are carried out properly, and, when they detect drink driving during work, to investigate the employer's responsibility, including whether a safe driving manager was appointed and how the duties were performed.

sections.heading: What training must a safe driving manager attend?

blocks.text: The company must have its safe driving manager and vice manager attend the statutory course whenever the Public Safety Commission notifies it. Article 74-3(9) of the Act creates the duty, and Article 108-2(1)(i) requires each Commission to run a course for safe driving managers.

Article 38(1) of the Enforcement Ordinance sets the content and length. The course covers traffic law, knowledge needed for safe driving, the knowledge and skills needed to give drivers traffic safety education, and the knowledge and skills of safe driving management. It must follow a course plan using textbooks and audiovisual materials, and each session runs 6 to 10 hours for a safe driving manager and 4 to 8 hours for a vice manager, depending on the size of the site and the person's experience.

The national law does not fix the interval; each Commission sends notices. The [Tokyo Metropolitan Police Department course page](https://www.keishicho.metro.tokyo.lg.jp/tetsuzuki/kotsu/drm/course.html) describes its course as held once every year, sends details by post to every registered manager, requires prior application and fee payment, and offers online or venue attendance.

Under Article 119-2, failing to appoint a manager or vice manager, or disobeying a Commission order to dismiss a manager or to take corrective measures, is punishable by a fine of up to 500,000 yen. The NPA notes that a 2022 amendment raised the fine from up to 50,000 yen, effective October 1, 2022.

The policy context is drink driving. The NPA reports in its [drink driving statistics](https://www.npa.go.jp/bureau/traffic/insyu/info.html) that there were 2,283 drink driving accidents in 2025, 125 of them fatal. The alcohol check duty extends to company cars a discipline that commercial carriers have long applied.

sections.heading: How should a company build its safe driving program?

items: Count vehicles at each site, counting motorcycles as half, and decide where managers and vice managers are needed.
Choose managers who meet the age and experience tests and give them written authority under Article 74-3(7).
Write an alcohol check procedure covering face to face and remote checks, designated assistants, and what happens when a driver tests positive.
Train designated assistants, since the NPA expects the manager to instruct them on the check method.
Track each manager's course notices and completion so no notice is missed.
Run driver education against the national guidelines and keep session records.

blocks.text: For the record keeping side see [how to prepare training records for an audit](/guides/how-to-prepare-training-records-for-an-audit) and [how long to keep training records](/guides/how-long-to-keep-training-records). Organizations with operations in the United States can compare this regime with [DOT drug and alcohol supervisor training](/regulations/dot-drug-and-alcohol-supervisor-training), and [Japan's broader workplace safety education duties](/regulations/japan-industrial-safety-and-health-act-training) apply alongside it.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry models each Article 9-10 duty as an obligation tied to the manager role, with separate outcomes for designated assistants who run alcohol checks. Course notices and completion become dated evidence linked to the obligation, so a site's compliance can be read from the framework rather than reconstructed from paper logs.

faqs.q: How are vehicles counted toward the five vehicle threshold?
faqs.a: Article 74-3 places the duty on the vehicle user (jidōsha no shiyōsha) and counts vehicles per base of use, with large and ordinary motorcycles counting as half a vehicle. How particular leased or shared vehicles are counted can depend on the facts, and the NPA directs questions to the prefectural police or police station with jurisdiction over the site.

The NPA Q&A says that roll calls, including alcohol checks, using devices certified for automatic roll calls under the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism's 2023 notice can be treated as equivalent to face to face checks. The device must be used as certified, without disabling any function.

faqs.q: What should happen if a driver tests positive?
faqs.a: The manager must stop the driver from driving. Where an assistant or another site's manager ran the check, the NPA Q&A says the result must be reported to the driver's own manager, who must instruct the driver to stop, directly or through the other site's manager.

faqs.q: Is the safe driving manager course available online?
faqs.a: Some Commissions offer it online. The Tokyo Metropolitan Police Department lets managers choose an online course or a venue course and asks those who can to attend online. Arrangements differ by prefecture, so follow the notice your Commission sends.
